display.purpose: Pinyon Script for names only: the couple in the hero and footer (in names ink), the nav monogram, and a guest party's name as the RSVP greeting.

headline.purpose: Cormorant Garamond italic 500, centred section titles in ink-strong.

lead.purpose: Cormorant Garamond italic for the invitation line under the names and the footer's 'With love,'.

invitation-caps.purpose: Cormorant Garamond caps for lines the invitation prints and the labels that name them: the hero date (0.14em; 0.06em under 360px), the opening line (0.14em; 0.08em under 560px), the hero venue line (0.1em; one venue per line, nowrap, clamp(0.9rem, 3.9vw, 1.0625rem) at 0.04em under 560px), venue card headings (1.125rem, 0.1em, 600, ink-strong) and the footer date (1.125rem, 0.1em, 500, ink-deep).

title.purpose: Cormorant 500 for RSVP step headings; weight 600 for venue names and guest legends.

body.purpose: Jost 400 at 1.0625rem / 1.65 for all running text and field values.

label.purpose: Jost 500 tracked caps for nav links (0.22em); meal tags at 0.2em. The only Jost caps on the site.

button.purpose: Jost 500 caps at 0.08em on every pill.

shadows.name: card-rest
shadows.purpose: Venue and RSVP cards: contact line, near lift, long low pool.

shadows.name: pill-hover
shadows.purpose: Filled pills on hover, with a 1px lift.

shadows.name: nav-scrolled
shadows.purpose: The nav once it fills on scroll, paired with saturate(1.2) blur(14px).

shadows.name: choice-selected
shadows.purpose: Doubles the ink border on a selected answer choice.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The single easing for blooms, rises and state changes.

motion.name: bloom
motion.purpose: Peony unfolds from its corner: circle clip-path 0% to 150% at the corner, opacity in, blur 6px clearing by 60%, scale 0.86 and rotate -5deg settling to rest.

motion.name: drift
motion.purpose: Inner layer translates 2px, -2px, out of phase with the sway; both pause while the hero is off screen.

motion.name: rise-in
motion.purpose: Hero lines enter from 14px below with a fade, in reading order.

motion.name: step-enter
motion.purpose: Each RSVP step and revealed sub-section rises in (rise-in keyframes).

motion.name: state
motion.value: 150ms fields, 160-200ms pills, 180ms choices, 300ms nav and cards

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion: plain fades replace bloom, rise and step-enter; no sway or drift; hover lifts removed; instant anchor scrolling.

narrative.overview:
The site is the printed invitation's world, not a picture of the invitation. The page itself is the card stock: a full-bleed ivory sheet (paper) that warms toward a soft ground below the hero, with faint blush glows pooled at left and right. The invitation's embossed white peonies are lifted off the print and set at the screen's own corners, top-left and bottom-right, so the browser window becomes the frame. The page closes the way the card does, on the bottom-right peony again at the footer.

Everything is set in one warm taupe-umber ink at five strengths, with three faces doing strictly separate jobs: a formal script for names, Cormorant Garamond for the invitation's voice, and Jost for everything a guest reads or taps. Interactive surfaces are soft and modern (28px cards, pill buttons, 14px fields) so the RSVP feels easy on a phone without breaking the stationery mood. Motion is a slow breath: the peonies bloom open, then sway in a light breeze.

The build was code-led with no image generation. The only imagery is the invitation's own peonies, extracted from the print by `scripts/extract-florals.mjs` as shadow-only alpha (the embossed shading without the white card), so they sit on any ground. These rasters are placeholders until the designer's original floral files arrive. The world explicitly refuses the card-on-a-page presentation (a framed invitation floating on a backdrop) and the stock wedding template's photo hero and countdown. The one borrowed device is the venue icon tile, kept by the user's choice to match the reference site thevanschatz.com: a single-stroke SVG in a blush circle heading each venue card.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed ivory page; no frame, no backdrop behind a card-shaped invitation.
Peonies anchored to the viewport corners in the hero, and to the bottom-right corner at the footer close.
One warm ink family at five strengths; no second hue except a muted terracotta for errors.
Script for names only; Cormorant for the invitation's voice; Jost for reading and tapping.
Soft, warm-shadowed cards and pill buttons for the functional parts.
Bloom, then breeze: entrance motion is slow and the idle motion is barely there.

rules.name: The Ink Ladder Rule
rules.body: All text and strokes come from one umber family, chosen by job: names (names), body (ink-deep), headings and buttons (ink-strong), secondary (muted), field strokes (control). Pick the step by role and contrast, never by mood.

rules.name: The Print Taupe Is Large Rule
rules.body: The invitation's literal taupe (ink) carries text only at script sizes. Anything under display size steps down to ink-deep or darker.

rules.name: The Names Only Rule
rules.body: Pinyon Script sets names and nothing else: the couple's names, their monogram, and a guest party's own name when greeting them. Never a heading, label, or decorative word.

rules.name: The Two Registers Rule
rules.body: Cormorant caps are for lines the invitation prints and the labels that name them (date, venues, the opening line, venue card headings, the footer date); Cormorant italic is for lines it speaks (section titles, the lead, "With love,"). Jost is for everything a guest reads to act or taps.

rules.name: The Screen Is the Card Rule
rules.body: Ornament anchors to the viewport's corners, not to a box inside the page. Peonies sit at top: 0 / left: 0 and right: 0 / bottom: 0 of full-width sections and bleed off the edge.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are always umber-tinted, long and soft, with negative spread. Ghost buttons, fields at rest and the page itself carry none.

dos: **Do** let the page be the invitation: full-bleed paper to ground gradient, peonies anchored at the viewport's corners and bleeding off the edge.

**Do** pick text color from the ink ladder by role: names ink for the couple's names (hero and footer), ink-deep for body, ink-strong for headings and buttons, muted for secondary lines, control for field strokes.

**Do** keep Pinyon Script for names only, Cormorant caps for printed invitation lines and their labels (venue headings, footer date), Cormorant italic for section titles and lead lines, and Jost for body, nav links, field labels and buttons.
**Do** head each venue card with its single-stroke icon in a 52px blush circle, and keep the device to the venue cards.
**Do** use 28px cards with the warm three-layer card shadow, pill buttons (filled for the main action, ghost beside it), and 14px fields at 52px tall.
**Do** tint every shadow umber (`rgb(94 68 48 / ...)`) and use expo-out easing for purposeful motion.
**Do** pause idle motion off screen and give every animation a plain-fade reduced-motion path.
**Do** keep reading text at 1.0625rem or larger and every target at 44px or taller.
donts: **Don't** present the invitation as a framed card or picture floating on a backdrop; the screen is the card.
**Don't** fall back to the stock wedding template's photo hero or countdown.
**Don't** set any heading, label or decorative word in Pinyon Script.
**Don't** use the print taupe (ink) for text below display size; it is 3.4:1.
**Don't** use neutral grey or black shadows, or shadows on the page itself.
**Don't** introduce a second accent hue; blush is a glow and a selection fill, terracotta is for errors only.
